links.outcome: Effect of removing structured clinical descriptors on guideline retrieval in grounded report generation
links.effect: Removing structured clinical descriptors substantially altered retrieved evidence; qualitative clinical framing influenced evidence selection more than numerical values alone. Full RAS pipeline performed best for LLaMA (NumCov 0.98±0.03).
links.quote: Structured clinical descriptors were essential for guideline selection: their removal substantially altered the retrieved evidence, demonstrating that qualitative clinical framing influenced evidence selection more strongly than numerical values alone.

links.outcome: Numerical faithfulness and directional bias of LLM-generated reports from simulation outputs
links.effect: Qwen frequently distorted simulation-derived values and under-reported time in range by mean -10.6 percentage points, over-reporting time below range and inflating hypoglycemia risk.
links.quote: Directional bias analysis showed that Qwen systematically under-reported time in range by a mean of -10.6 percentage points and over-reported time below range, thereby inflating hypoglycemia risk.

links.outcome: Report accuracy against simulation ground truth across two LLMs using rubric and numerical coverage
links.effect: LLaMA full pipeline maintained high numerical faithfulness (NumCov 0.98±0.03), while Qwen showed substantial model-specific safety risks; findings consistent across two evaluators (score difference >2.1).
links.quote: However, aggregate framework scores alone are insufficient for clinical validation.
